examples.en: Please knock first before you go in.
He knocked quietly on the door.
Even when I knock on the meeting room door, there is no answer.

examples.ko: 사장님 방에 들어갈 때는 노크해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to knock when you enter the boss's office.
I heard the sound of someone knocking on the door.
I knocked and waited, but nobody came out.

explain: '문을 노크하다'처럼 '문을'과 함께 써요. 영어 knock에서 온 말이라 일상에서도 '문을 두드리다'보다 '노크하다'를 더 자주 말해요. '두드리다'는 세게 여러 번 칠 때 써요. 소리를 말할 때는 '노크 소리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It goes with '문을', as in '문을 노크하다'. It comes from English 'knock', and in daily talk people say '노크하다' more often than '문을 두드리다'. '두드리다' is for hitting hard, several times. For the sound, people say '노크 소리'.

examples.en: Please dress neatly in front of adults.
I tied my hair neatly and went to the interview.

examples.ko: 학생들이 교복을 단정히 입고 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: The students lined up wearing their uniforms neatly.
I tidied up the desk neatly.

examples.ko: 그는 늘 단정히 앉아서 이야기를 들어요.
examples.en: He always sits properly and listens to the story.
Since guests were there, I straightened my appearance neatly.

explain: 옷, 머리, 자세, 정리 상태가 흐트러짐 없이 바를 때 써요. '깔끔하게'와 비슷하지만 단정히는 예의 바르고 반듯한 느낌이 더 강해요. 보통 '입다, 앉다, 하다'와 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when clothes, hair, posture or arrangement are in good order. It is similar to '깔끔하게', but 단정히 has a stronger feel of being proper and well-mannered. It usually goes with verbs like '입다', '앉다' and '하다'.

examples.en: In winter, wearing extra socks keeps my feet warm.

examples.ko: 신발 안에 보이지 않는 덧신을 신었어요.
examples.en: I wore no-show socks inside my shoes.
The footies keep slipping off, which is annoying.
I bought footies and sneakers together.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 신발 위에 덧신을 신었어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day I put overshoes on top of my shoes.

examples.ko: 선물로 귀여운 덧신을 한 켤레 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a pair of cute footies as a gift.

explain: 신발이나 양말 위에 덧신는 것을 말하고, 발목이 안 보이게 짧은 양말을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. 한 켤레, 두 켤레로 세고 '신다, 벗다'와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It means something worn over shoes or socks, and it is also commonly used for very short socks that don't show at the ankle. Count them with '켤레' and use verbs like '신다' and '벗다'.

en: looking around; glancing this way and that

examples.ko: 아이가 낯선 곳에서 두리번두리번 주위를 살폈어요.
examples.en: The child looked around this way and that in the unfamiliar place.
I looked all around, but I couldn't see my wallet.

examples.ko: 신입생이 교실 앞에서 두리번두리번 누군가를 찾았어요.
examples.en: The new student looked around in front of the classroom for someone.

examples.ko: 강아지가 두리번두리번 둘러보더니 제 옆에 앉았어요.
examples.en: The puppy glanced around and then sat next to me.

examples.ko: 관광객이 지도를 들고 두리번두리번 거리를 둘러봐요.
examples.en: A tourist holding a map looks around the street in all directions.
While looking around here and there, my eyes met my friend's.

explain: 고개를 이리저리 돌리며 주변을 살피는 모습이에요. 대화에서는 '두리번거리다'라고 동사로 많이 말하니 함께 알아 두세요. 길을 찾거나 누군가를 찾을 때, 낯선 곳에서 어색할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes turning your head this way and that to look around. In conversation the verb '두리번거리다' is commonly used, so learn it together. It suits situations like looking for a way or a person, or feeling awkward in an unfamiliar place.

examples.en: He slung his backpack over his shoulder and went to the mountain.
Please sling the bag over one shoulder.
My father shouldered a shovel and went out to the field.
Now that I've slung the load over my shoulder, it's heavier than I thought.
A student with a guitar slung over his shoulder walked by.
Why did you sling such a big backpack over your shoulder?

explain: '메다'를 조금 길게 한 말이라, 말할 때는 그냥 '메다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 가방, 배낭, 삽처럼 어깨 위로 올리는 물건과 써요. 손에 들 때는 '들다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a slightly longer form of '메다', and in speech plain '메다' sounds far more natural. It goes with things you put over the shoulder, like bags, backpacks and shovels. When you hold something in your hand, use '들다'.

examples.en: He silently kept turning his ring around and around.

examples.ko: 아이가 옷자락을 만지작만지작 만지며 눈치를 봐요.
examples.en: The child fiddles with the hem of their clothes while watching others' reactions.

examples.ko: 할머니는 손수건을 만지작만지작 접었다 폈다 하세요.
examples.en: Grandma keeps folding and unfolding her handkerchief with her fingers.
With a worried face, I rolled my pen around in my fingers.
I was fiddling around and broke the cup.

examples.ko: 아기가 털실 뭉치를 만지작만지작 갖고 놀아요.
examples.en: The baby plays with the ball of yarn, fiddling with it.

explain: 말없이 손만 움직이는 모습이라 긴장, 고민, 심심함이 느껴져요. '만지작만지작 돌리다', '만지작만지작 굴리다'처럼 뒤에 오는 동작을 꾸며요. 손을 쓰는 작은 물건과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It shows hands moving without words, so you can feel nervousness, worry or boredom. It modifies the action that follows, as in '만지작만지작 돌리다' or '만지작만지작 굴리다'. It goes well with small objects handled by hand.

examples.ko: 대통령 초청 만찬회가 저녁 일곱 시에 열려요.
examples.en: The banquet hosted by the president is held at seven in the evening.
The company decided to hold a New Year banquet.
To attend the banquet, you have to wear a formal suit.

examples.ko: 졸업생을 위한 만찬회는 학교 식당에서 열렸어요.
examples.en: The banquet for the graduates was held in the school cafeteria.

examples.ko: 어제 만찬회에서 오랜만에 옛 친구를 만났어요.
examples.en: At the banquet yesterday, I met an old friend after a long time.

examples.ko: 만찬회 준비 때문에 요리사들이 아침부터 바빠요.
examples.en: The chefs have been busy since morning preparing for the banquet.

explain: '만찬'이 더 자주 쓰이고, 만찬회는 행사나 뉴스에서 모임 자체를 강조할 때 보여요. 초청받아 가는 공식 저녁 자리에 어울리고, 친구끼리 먹는 평범한 저녁에는 쓰지 않아요. 점심 자리는 '오찬'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '만찬' is used more often, and 만찬회 appears in events and news when the focus is on the gathering itself. It suits formal invited dinners, not an ordinary dinner among friends. A formal lunch is called '오찬'.

examples.en: The doors to the rooms in our house are sliding doors.
Slide the door open and go in.
The wardrobe has sliding doors, so it takes up less space.

examples.ko: 미닫이 창문이 뻑뻑해서 잘 안 열려요.
examples.en: The sliding window is stiff and doesn't open easily.
In a small room, a sliding door is more convenient than a swing door.
I changed the bathroom door to a sliding one.

explain: 옆으로 밀어서 여는 문이나 창을 말해요. 앞뒤로 당기거나 밀어서 여는 문은 '여닫이'라고 해서 짝으로 알아 두면 좋아요. '미닫이문', '미닫이 창'처럼 뒤에 '문'이나 '창'을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a door or window that opens by sliding sideways. A door that swings open by pushing or pulling is called '여닫이', so it helps to learn them as a pair. You can also add '문' or '창' after it, as in '미닫이문' and '미닫이 창'.

examples.ko: 첫 출근날 어리바리 헤매다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: On my first day at work, I wandered around in a daze and got lost.
Everyone goes around a bit lost when they're new.
I wasn't fully awake, so I answered in a daze.

examples.ko: 어리바리 서 있지 말고 이쪽으로 와요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there dazed; come over here.
On my first trip abroad, I wandered around feeling bewildered.

examples.ko: 그는 어리바리 앉아 있다가 버스를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: He sat there spaced out and missed the bus.

explain: 정신이 없고 서툴러 보이는 모습에 쓰는 구어체 말이에요. 친구나 동료끼리 편하게 말할 때 어울리고, 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It is a colloquial word for looking dazed and clumsy. It suits casual talk between friends or coworkers, and is not used much in formal settings.

examples.en: My younger sibling is absorbed in preparing for the exam.
The kids are completely absorbed in their game.
Mom was fully occupied with washing the dishes.

examples.ko: 요즘 회사 사람들은 새 제품 홍보에 여념이 없어요.
examples.en: These days, people at the company are busy promoting the new product.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에도 농부들은 일에 여념이 없어요.
examples.en: Even on rainy days, the farmers are hard at work.

examples.ko: 그는 책 읽기에 여념 없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat there absorbed in reading his book.

explain: 거의 '~에 여념이 없다' 모양으로 써서, 한 가지 일에 푹 빠져 다른 생각을 할 틈이 없다는 뜻이 돼요. '바쁘다'와 달리 그 일에 몰두하는 모습에 초점이 있고, 앞에는 몰두하는 일을 '-에'로 붙여요.

phrases.en: The students are busy with graduation preparations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어를 따로 풀면 뜻이 잘 안 잡히지만, 이 굳은 표현으로 '한 일에 몰두하다'가 돼요. 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word alone does not reveal this meaning, but this set phrase means being engrossed in one task. It is common in writing and news.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '~에 여념이 없다', meaning someone is so absorbed in one thing that they have no room for other thoughts. Unlike '바쁘다' (busy), it focuses on being immersed in the task, and the task is marked with '-에' before it.

examples.en: Bookstores arrange their books by genre.

examples.ko: 마트에서는 인기 있는 상품을 입구 쪽에 진열해요.
examples.en: Supermarkets display popular products near the entrance.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 신발을 가게 앞에 진열하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are putting the newly released shoes on display in front of the store.

examples.ko: 유리 상자 안에 보석을 예쁘게 진열했어요.
examples.en: They displayed the jewels nicely inside a glass case.

examples.ko: 가게 주인이 과일을 색깔별로 진열하는 중이에요.
examples.en: The shop owner is arranging the fruit by color.

examples.ko: 상품을 보기 좋게 진열하면 더 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: If you display products attractively, they sell better.

explain: '전시하다'와 달리 가게에서 팔 물건을 보기 좋게 늘어놓을 때 많이 써요. 박물관이나 전시회에서 작품을 보여 줄 때는 '전시하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 물건이 놓여 있는 상태는 '진열되어 있다'로 말하고, 물건을 올려 두는 선반은 '진열대'라고 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '전시하다', it is mostly used for goods arranged to be sold in a shop. For artworks at a museum or exhibition, '전시하다' sounds more natural. The state of things being on display is '진열되어 있다', and the shelf is called a '진열대'.

en: congratulatory or condolence flowers; flower stand; wreath

examples.ko: 개업 축하 화환이 가게 앞에 줄지어 있었어요.
examples.en: Congratulatory flower stands were lined up in front of the new shop.

examples.ko: 친구 아버지 장례식에 보낼 화환을 골랐어요.
examples.en: I chose a wreath to send to my friend's father's funeral.

examples.ko: 결혼식장 입구에 화환 몇 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A few flower stands are standing at the entrance of the wedding hall.

examples.ko: 축하 화환에는 보낸 사람 이름이 적힌 띠가 있어요.
examples.en: A congratulatory flower stand has a ribbon with the sender's name on it.

examples.ko: 화환으로 마음을 전하는 문화가 한국에는 있어요.
examples.en: In Korea there is a custom of conveying your feelings with a flower stand.

examples.ko: 화환은 행사가 끝나면 다른 곳에 다시 쓰기도 해요.
examples.en: After an event, flower stands are sometimes reused somewhere else.

explain: 한국에서는 개업, 결혼식, 장례식에 키가 큰 꽃 장식을 보내요. 축하할 때는 '축하 화환', 장례식에는 '근조 화환'이라고 앞말을 바꿔요. 동그란 꽃 고리보다 세워 두는 꽃 장식을 먼저 떠올리는 사람이 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea people send tall flower arrangements for shop openings, weddings, and funerals. You change the first word: '축하 화환' for congratulations and '근조 화환' for a funeral. Many Koreans picture a standing flower display before a round flower ring.
